plan: Model the session as a single dictionary with exactly the four contract keys, reset from one initial-state template so begin/abandon produce identical clean states.

Dispatch handle() through a mapping from action type to a per-action handler; each handler validates preconditions and payload types completely before any mutation, returning an 'Error: ...' screen on failure so accepted data is never corrupted and nothing raises.

Derive prompts from a single _state_prompt() function (completed -> 'Check-in complete', unconfirmed contact -> 'Confirm contact', no appointment -> 'Choose appointment', else 'Review and complete'), used for corrections and error screens; emit the contract's fixed prompts explicitly for choice, completion, and abandon.

Build every screen through one _screen() factory that returns fresh dicts and attaches copied appointment choices in input order exactly when the prompt is 'Choose appointment', otherwise an empty list.
Copy the appointments sequence (and each entry) at construction and keep an id set for O(1) validation, checking isinstance(str) before membership so unhashable inputs cannot raise.

Implement run_once() to raise RuntimeError before calling anything if action_source or screen_sink is missing, then perform exactly one read_action(), one handle(), one display(), and return the same screen object, so standard-library unittest fakes with those two methods suffice.
mechanisms: single authoritative session dictionary with template-based reset
type-keyed handler dispatch with validate-then-mutate discipline
centralized screen factory enforcing the choices/prompt invariant with defensive copies
constructor-time appointment copy plus id-set validation
duck-typed injected action source and screen sink with fail-fast RuntimeError in run_once
